subject: Business Models
title: Evernote's Decline
description: A fast breakdown of Evernote's Decline for builders.

hook.text: Evernote was once valued at $1 billion. Its CEO called it a '100-year company.' It sold for $225 million.

buildup.text: Evernote's free tier was too generous: unlimited notes, device sync, web clipper—all free.

discovery.text: With 225 million users and only 7.7 million paying, Evernote couldn't fund product development. Quality stalled.

twist.text: Evernote then restricted free features too aggressively. Angry free users left instead of converting.

climax.text: Evernote's lesson: too-generous free tiers kill conversion. Too-harsh restrictions kill the user base.

punchline.text: $1B valuation, sold for $225M. Free was too generous, then too restrictive.

quiz.question: What was Evernote's fundamental freemium mistake?
options: Free tier was too generous, killing conversion
Not having a free tier at all

details.summary: Evernote was one of the earliest freemium success stories with 225 million users, but it collapsed by giving too much away for free while failing to build compelling premium features. Users had no reason to upgrade, the product stagnated, and competitors like Notion absorbed its user base.
details.whyItMatters: Evernote is the cautionary tale of freemium done wrong. It demonstrates that a massive free user base is worthless without strong conversion, continuous product improvement, and a clear premium value proposition that evolves with customer needs.
takeaways: 225 million users could not save Evernote from financial decline
The free tier was too generous, eliminating the motivation to upgrade
Product stagnation allowed focused competitors to steal paying users

faq.question: What specific mistakes did Evernote make with its freemium model?
faq.answer: The free tier included nearly everything most users needed. Premium features like offline access and PDF annotation did not justify the price for casual users. The company expanded into hardware and unrelated products instead of improving core note-taking..

faq.question: What lessons should freemium companies learn from Evernote?
faq.answer: A large free user base is not inherently valuable without conversion. Continuous product innovation is essential to maintain premium value. Focus on deepening the core product rather than expanding into unrelated areas..
